compiled_state.title: Opus remediation sub-agents at strategic review points
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural

## Context

When dso:completion-verifier returns non-PASS mid-sprint, the operator running /dso:sprint today reads a bug-task body that the orchestrator drafted inline from a 1-3 line remediation_tasks_created hint — a body missing the AC scaffolding, TDD specs, dependency chains, and structured reasoning that the original dso:task-decomposer (opus) embedded in the parent story's tasks. The same drop in fidelity happens upstream: in /dso:preplanning Phase E, when red-team/blue-team return findings, the orchestrator transcribes them into new story bodies and DD modifications without the INVEST coverage and SC-traceability the original dso:story-decomposer applied. In /dso:implementation-plan Steps 2/4/6, the same pattern repeats for approach proposals, task drafts, and gap-analysis amendments. The sprint operator must mentally reconstruct the intended scope from these thin remediation artifacts, and downstream sub-agent batches inherit weaker context to act on — compounding the quality loss across cycles.

Stakeholder: the sprint operator (the engineer running /dso:sprint), who today carries the mental burden of patching low-fidelity remediation back to original-task fidelity before dispatching downstream sub-agents. Secondarily: the downstream sub-agents themselves, which produce lower-quality implementations when fed weaker remediation context.

Change after this ships: the operator sees remediation artifacts at the same fidelity as the original opus producer — bug tasks have full AC + TDD + dependencies; modified DDs match the original DD format; new stories have full INVEST + done-definition coverage. The operator no longer mentally patches; downstream sub-agents receive consistent-fidelity context.

## Success Criteria

- SC1 When dso:red-team-reviewer/dso:blue-team-filter return non-empty findings in preplanning Phase E, the orchestrator re-dispatches dso:story-decomposer (model: "opus") with a remediation_context payload referencing reviewer artifacts by absolute file path. The producer operates in delta-mode: emits only new/modified stories under a branched "DELTA OUTPUT" template, never a full re-decomposition. Pre-generation gate: the producer must Read each path in remediation_context and quote evidence from each before emitting output (orchestrator transcription is prohibited). Verified by: synthetic-findings fixture asserting (a) Task subagent_type and model, (b) payload contains file paths not embedded finding bodies, (c) producer output contains a "DELTA OUTPUT" mode declaration and evidence quotes from each reviewer artifact before the story drafts, (d) stories not named in any finding's target_story_id are absent from the producer's output.

- SC2 When architectural reviewers fail Step 2 or Step 4 of /dso:implementation-plan, or when the Step 6 gap-analyzer returns findings, the orchestrator re-dispatches the corresponding producer (dso:approach-proposer for Step 2; dso:task-decomposer for Steps 4 and 6) with model: "opus" and a remediation_context payload passing reviewer artifacts by absolute file path. Producers operate in delta-mode with the same DELTA OUTPUT template, mode declaration, and pre-generation Read gate as SC1. Verified by: per-touchpoint test fixtures asserting the dispatch shape, by-reference payload, mode declaration, evidence quotes, and delta-mode preservation of prior tasks/AC.

- SC3 When dso:completion-verifier returns P1 != PASS at any dispatch site (story-level Phase F Step 18, epic-level Phase G Step 2, or d039-ac65 re-dispatch), the orchestrator dispatches dso:verification-remediation-planner (opus) before any remediation ticket is written. The planner reads the verifier's full output directly (criteria_results, evidence_searched, remediation_tasks_created). The planner classifies remediation scope using a deterministic ordered decision tree (1: zero AC evidence for any criterion -> replan_story; 2: all criteria have partial evidence + gap is implementation-only -> new_tasks_in_story; 3: criterion requires new user-facing behavior not in current story -> new_story_in_epic; 4: criteria span multiple epics -> replan_epic). The planner emits {scope, target_id, decomposer_context, escalation_upstream, confidence}. Confidence is LOW only when two rules tie after tiebreakers. The orchestrator dispatches the indicated decomposer with decomposer_context, OR (when confidence == LOW) halts with HALT_FOR_USER surfacing the planner's evidence. Verified by: sprint end-to-end test injecting synthetic verifier outputs that exercise each branch of the decision tree.

- SC4 The remediation loop at every touchpoint emits a "Current cycle: N of MAX_CYCLES" declaration at iteration start. It terminates within MAX_CYCLES (default 3 via planning.max_remediation_cycles; minimum enforced >= 2) — success on any cycle -> continue; OR emit REPLAN_ESCALATE: <upstream> on cycle MAX_CYCLES failure with <upstream> set per cascade mapping (brainstorm for Phase E; preplanning for impl-plan Steps 2/4/6; the planner's escalation_upstream for verifier-fail). /dso:oscillation-check is a hard gate on cycle >= 2; skipping requires explicit OSCILLATION_CHECK_SKIPPED: <reason> ticket comment. On detected oscillation, the loop halts with OSCILLATION_HALT. HALT_FOR_USER (planner low confidence) and REPLAN_ESCALATE (cycle exhaustion) are structurally exclusive: REPLAN_ESCALATE may only be emitted when cycle_count == MAX_CYCLES AND findings is non-empty; other states emit PROTOCOL_ERROR. Verified by: forced-failing-review fixture asserting exactly 3 dispatches with cycle declarations, no cycle 4, correct REPLAN_ESCALATE shape; oscillation fixture; HALT-vs-REPLAN exclusivity fixture.

- SC5 Each remediation cycle appends an entry to the touchpoint's existing review artifact under a cycles: [{n, draft_hash, findings_count, verdict, timestamp_iso}] array with atomic-append (concurrent writers do not lose entries). The array is initialized to [] when reading an existing in-flight artifact that lacks the key (graceful migration). A single ticket comment references the artifact path. Verified by: each touchpoint's existing review-artifact test extended to assert the cycles array; concurrent-write fixture asserting no entries are lost; migration fixture (artifact without cycles[] pre-existing) asserting graceful initialization.

## State Lifecycle

| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| remediation_context payload (shape: docs/contracts/remediation-context.md) | Loop driver in each touchpoint (preplanning Phase E; impl-plan Steps 2/4/6) and verifier-fail dispatcher in sprint construct the payload before each producer re-dispatch; payload references reviewer artifacts by absolute path, never embedded finding bodies | Re-constructed each cycle (new findings; cycle_number incremented; oscillation_hints when cycle >= 2) | Producer agents (story-decomposer, task-decomposer, approach-proposer) Read paths via pre-generation gate; verification-remediation-planner consumes verifier output to construct | Transient — one loop's lifetime only; not persisted across sessions |
| cycles[] array in review artifacts (extends $ARTIFACTS_DIR/adversarial-review-<epic-id>.json for Phase E; new sibling files at impl-plan touchpoints and verifier-fail path) | Loop driver appends entry on cycle 1; initializes to [] for in-flight pre-existing artifacts | Atomic-append per cycle | Future-cycle reviewers consult oscillation_hints; post-mortem and calibration tooling read for audit | Persists per-epic; cleaned only on epic deletion |
| planning.max_remediation_cycles config key (default 3, min 2; .claude/dso-config.conf) | Operator writes once at project setup; default baked into plugins/dso/hooks/lib/planning-config.sh | Operator edits | Loop driver in each touchpoint reads at loop entry | Removed only if knob retired |
| REPLAN_ESCALATE: <upstream> ticket comment | Loop driver writes on cycle MAX_CYCLES failure with correct upstream skill name | N/A (immutable) | Upstream skill (brainstorm, preplanning, implementation-plan) reads on re-entry; counted against existing sprint.max_replan_cycles cap | Read at most once per upstream re-entry; persists as audit trail |
| New agent file plugins/dso/agents/verification-remediation-planner.md | Created in this epic | Edited via standard plugin-edit workflow | Read by sprint dispatcher at each completion-verifier non-PASS site | Removed only if the planner pattern retired |

## Dependencies
None.

## Approach

Option A: Skill-Local Loop with Shared Protocol Doc. Each skill (preplanning, impl-plan, sprint) embeds the loop logic inline at its review touchpoint(s), pulling protocol details from a new shared workflow doc skills/shared/workflows/remediation-loop-protocol.md (mirrors DSO's existing epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md pattern). New dso:verification-remediation-planner (opus) is the canonical handler for every completion-verifier non-PASS verdict; optional remediation_context input added to existing dso:story-decomposer, dso:task-decomposer, dso:approach-proposer; new config key planning.max_remediation_cycles=3.

## Scenario Analysis

Critical
- New planner missing from older plugin cache (deployment): fallback path defined via existing graceful-degradation pattern (general-purpose + inline agent file content).
- Phase E story-map overwrite risk (assumption): addressed in SC1 via delta-mode + DELTA OUTPUT template.
- Sonnet constructing remediation_context undermines the epic premise (assumption): addressed in SC1/SC2 via by-reference payload (file paths, not transcribed bodies).

High
- Opus dispatch storms under throttle tier (runtime): loop driver runs usage-tier preflight per cycle; on MAX_AGENTS=0 emit explicit halt, not silent stall.
- Concurrent verifier + Phase E cycles[] write race (runtime): addressed in SC5 via atomic-append.
- Opus timeout silent inline fallback (runtime): protocol must specify timeout handling (retry / REPLAN_ESCALATE); inline fallback prohibited.
- Planner mis-classification (runtime): addressed in SC3 via ordered decision tree + confidence + HALT_FOR_USER.
- Producer non-determinism + reviewer mis-calibration cause loops never to converge (assumption): addressed in SC4 via oscillation-check integration.
- cycles=0/1 disables loop (configuration): SC4 enforces minimum >= 2.
- Cascade-cap collision (configuration): planner's escalation_upstream counts against existing sprint.max_replan_cycles cap.
- REPLAN_ESCALATE upstream criterion (configuration): addressed in SC3 — planner emits escalation_upstream as part of classification.
- Verifier hints insufficient signal for planner (assumption): addressed in SC3 — planner reads evidence_searched, not just hints.
- Planner-induced loops (assumption): planner self-check field included; mis-classifications detected by next verifier dispatch (existing pattern).
- In-flight artifacts without cycles[] schema (deployment): addressed in SC5 via graceful migration.
- Producer non-determinism (assumption): SC4 oscillation-check provides convergence safeguard.

Medium
- Protocol doc namespace path correctness (deployment): enforce _PLUGIN_ROOT references in touchpoint skills.
- Config key registration in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md (deployment): preplanning task.
- remediation_context payload size unbounded (configuration): cap payload, prioritize critical findings, or chunk cycles.

## Prompt Alignment Findings

dso:bot-psychologist review (sonnet) surfaced 5 behavioral-soundness concerns, all folded into SCs as explicit design constraints:
- Q1 Critical (delta-mode): Branched DELTA OUTPUT template + mandatory mode-declaration self-check — folded into SC1, SC2.
- Q2 High (by-reference comprehension): Pre-generation Read gate with evidence quotation — folded into SC1, SC2.
- Q3 High (planner classifier): Ordered decision tree with tiebreakers (replaces free-form classification) — folded into SC3.
- Q4 High (cross-touchpoint consistency): "Current cycle: N of MAX_CYCLES" declaration + oscillation-check skip-justification — folded into SC4.
- Q5 Medium (HALT_FOR_USER vs REPLAN_ESCALATE): Structural exclusivity via cycle_count preconditions — folded into SC4.

## Cross-Epic Scan

SKIPPED — infrastructure block on cross-epic-scan-prep.sh (filed as bug 701a-2b89-3486-47cb). User-authorized skip per 2026-05-22 Jira-bridge brainstorm precedent. Practical risk low: epic touches sub-agent dispatch behavior in 3 skills + 3 existing decomposer agents; no known concurrent epics modify those same files in scope.
